Log employee change by condition Checks of data quality, response IDs, IP addresses, and response durations were used to evaluate and ensure the independence of observations. Levene’s test showed that the assumption of homogeneity of variances was met: F(3, 176) = 1.55, p = 0.20. However, assumption checks indicated that the residentials significantly deviated from normality, as assessed by the Shapiro- Wilk test: W = 0.97, p = 0.001. Because residuals deviated from normality, we conducted a two-way analysis of variance using heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors, which provide valid inference under non- normality and heteroskedasticity. A two-way analysis of variance was conducted to examine the effects of priming (general versus local) and framing (quality versus energy efficiency) on the projected log change in the number of employees. The main effect of priming was not significant: F(1, 176) = 1.40, p = 0.24. The main effect of framing was also not significant: F(1, 176) = 0.03, p = 0.85. The priming and framing interaction was likewise nonsignificant: F(1, 176) = 0.55, p = 0.46. 33 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
